text:
maya: Quick Q — seeing cascading 503s from inference v2 in prod-us-east. Who is authorized to flip the emergency disable for the inference feature flag? Also need the exact command and how we ensure the audit trail. I want to disable only the canary audience (us-east) while we debug.
 tom: Per runbook: oncall (current oncall) or an eng-sre lead can flip. Full prod-wide disables need SRE + Platform signoff. Canary-scoped flips (region/route) can be done by oncall alone but log the reason. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/feature-flip
 lia: Command we use (infra-cli):
```
infra flags set --env=prod --region=us-east --flag=inference_v2 --state=off --note="503 cascade observed, disabling canary"
```
Make sure to include a short note (reason) — that gets copied into the audit log. Also create a quick Jira ticket (INC-####) and tag @eng-oncall. For full-prod disables follow the two-person approval in the runbook.
 ops-bot: audit: flag-change recorded (id: 7f9d3c2a). All flips trigger append-only audit entries in the control-plane log and a KMS-signed event. Deploy notifications posted to #deploys.
 jonathan: If you flip the canary, also point traffic to fallback variant to avoid user-facing errors: 
```
redwood route set --service=inference --variant=fallback-v1 --region=us-east
```
I'll standby to approve any broader action — I'm on-call for the next hour. If this becomes a larger outage escalate to SRE lead @tom and follow the incident checklist.
 maya: ok doing the canary flip now, will paste the infra-cli output and INC ticket here. thanks :thumbsup:
 tom: +1. After flip, confirm metrics (5xx rate, latency) and let #incidents know. We should also mark this as "emergency-disable" in the postmortem checklist so it appears in the RCA.
